title: Obex sits atop a three-layer structure of Agent, Prime Foundation, and development company
content:
The Agent Creation Primitive's parameters name two off-chain entities. "Rubicon is the Prime Foundation associated with Obex. Its mandate is to support the development, growth, and adoption of Obex" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.1.5). "Treadstone is the development company that provides services to Rubicon" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.1.6).

The contracting chain is the detail worth noticing: Treadstone serves **Rubicon**, not Obex. The Agent is an Atlas-governed construct with on-chain accounts; the Foundation is the legal person that can hold contracts and employ people; the development company is a supplier to that legal person. Each layer contracts only with its neighbour.

This insulates the Agent from direct commercial relationships. Obex's Artifact governs the Foundation's mandate, not the terms of Treadstone's engagement — so a change of development company does not require an Artifact edit, while a change to the Foundation's mandate does.

The trade-off is oversight distance. Sky Governance reaches the Foundation through the Artifact, but reaches the actual builders only indirectly, through Rubicon's contracting discretion. Naming Treadstone in the Artifact at all is a partial answer to that: the supplier is at least disclosed on the record even though its terms are not.
description: Rubicon is the Prime Foundation mandated to support Obex's development, growth and adoption; Treadstone is the development company that provides services to Rubicon, not to Obex directly.
